subject: GPU min-floor & onramp timetable — HelixAI dedicated options
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sara Park <sara@helixai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Framing HelixAI dedicated options — initial cluster sizing notes

Sara — good talking yesterday. Per our discussion I wanted to put a short note on the table with three practical dedicated reservation pathways so your engineering and finance teams can reason about cost, activation risk, and SLA guarantees. I attached a quick usage snapshot (helixai_usage_snapshot.csv) from your trial and a sketch of the onramp diagram.

Summary (high level):
- Small baseline (min-floor): 16 A100-equivalent GPUs. Target for steady low-latency interactive inference and nightly batch jobs. Conservatively sized for current prod token rate.
- Growth lane (staggered ramp): start at 16, move to 48 over 6 months with checkpoints at 30 and 42 GPUs tied to traffic/quality signals.
- Performance lane (burstable + reserved): 48 reserved + 24 burstable for peak windows; reserved floor remains 48.

Key constraints to confirm from your side: 1) tolerance for warmup credits (we typically offer 4 weeks of reduced burn for activation), 2) whether you can tolerate auto-fallback to a quantized variant during multi-region outages, and 3) whether procurement wants an explicit SLA uplift for the first 90 days.

Action: can you confirm which pathway HelixAI prefers for proposal framing? If agreeable I’ll put together an explicit monthly cost table, activation timeline, and a canary plan that pins model variants for the first 30 days.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: helixai_usage_snapshot.csv (CSV, 120KB), proposed_onramp_diagram.pdf (diagram, 1 page)
From: Sara Park <sara@helixai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom@helixai.com>, procurement@helixai.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Framing HelixAI dedicated options — initial cluster sizing notes

Marcus — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. This is exactly what the team needed to start internal alignment. A few notes from our side after a quick review: 

- The usage snapshot looks right. We currently sustain a 95th percentile token/sec that maps to ~20 A100-equivalent GPUs for interactive traffic during PDT business hours, but batch jobs run overnight and spike aggregate consumption.
- Procurement asked for two pricing anchors: (A) a conservative baseline where we can scale up quickly, and (B) a performance floor where our SLOs are guaranteed.
- On warmup credits: finance will want explicit credit weeks in the commercial term. Three to four weeks preferred.
- On rollback and fallback: engineering prefers automatically routed fallback to a quantized variant rather than global degradation. We'll need that spelled out in the runbook.

Can you send a short matrix that maps: cluster size -> minimum reserved GPUs -> expected latency profile (p50/p95) -> warmup window? If you include a timeline (weeks to full activation) that would be great.

Tom, procurement — looping you in so you can flag any commercial items.

Best,
Sara Park
Head of Platform Engineering | HelixAI
sara@helixai.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Park <sara@helixai.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Framing HelixAI dedicated options — initial cluster sizing notes

Marcus / Lauren — following up with a quick draft matrix below that we can share with Helix. I kept it compact so procurement can parse quickly and engineering has the activation windows. I also added a canary plan suggestion and the fallback behavior. Please review and edit as needed before I convert to a spreadsheet.

Draft matrix (cluster -> min-reserved -> target p50/p95 latency -> activation timeframe)
- 16 GPUs -> 16 reserved -> p50 ~45ms / p95 ~130ms -> 1 week baseline activation (warmup credits: 2 weeks)
- 32 GPUs -> 24 reserved -> p50 ~35ms / p95 ~100ms -> 3 week activation (warmup credits: 3 weeks)
- 48 GPUs -> 48 reserved -> p50 ~28ms / p95 ~70ms -> 6 week activation (warmup credits: 4 weeks)

Canary plan: 1) deploy 10% traffic to dedicated lane for 72 hours, 2) monitor top-10 prompts latency and token consumption, 3) scale to 50% traffic if no regression, 4) cold-start / KV cache warm-ups handled by preloading top 500 prefixes during the warmup window.

Fallback: automatic routing to quantized variant (identical model weights, int8) if regional capacity falls below 60% of reserved floor; customers keep reserved floor and pay reduced rate for burst usage. We include an optional SLA uplift clause (first 90 days) with a targeted latency SLO tied to rolling 1h windows.

I will prepare the cost table once Marcus confirms the numeric anchors and we choose the pathway.

-Karthik
Director, Product Solutions | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sara Park <sara@helixai.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom@helixai.com>, procurement@helixai.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Nov 2026 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Framing HelixAI dedicated options — initial cluster sizing notes

Sara / Tom / procurement team — appreciate the rapid feedback. Per internal sync with Karthik and Lauren, we propose packaging two formal options for the commercial proposal:

Option 1 — Conservative Onramp (Recommended for short-term budget control)
- Initial cluster: 16 GPUs (A100-eq) reserved floor
- Activation: 1 week to baseline, warmup credit: 2 weeks free usage credit
- Ramp: ability to trigger tranche to 32 GPUs within 30 days (manual exec; 3 day activation SLA)
- SLA: standard support; SLA uplift available as add-on

Option 2 — Performance Baseline (Recommended for production SLOs)
- Initial cluster: 32 GPUs reserved (24 guaranteed, 8 soft-burst)
- Activation: 3 week activation with 3 weeks warmup credit
- Ramp: staged to 48 GPUs over 6 months, milestones at month 2 and month 4
- SLA: 99.9% availability on dedicated control plane + optional 30ms p50 target add-on for first 90 days

Common items:
- We will include a canary playbook (as Karthik outlined) and an automated fallback to quantized variant when capacity dips below 60% of reserved floor.
- Attachments: cost table and a more detailed activation diagram will follow in a separate spreadsheet.

Next steps: 1) Sara / Tom — please confirm which option to include in the initial SOW and if procurement needs a multi-year pricing anchor; 2) Marcus/Karthik/Lauren to draft SOW and cost sheet once Helix confirms pathway.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
